title: Real-time interactive
note: Installations that respond to a person in the room — touch, gesture, movement or voice. The audience is the input.

applications.name: Interactive Art Wall
applications.headline: The guest becomes the artwork.
applications.description: A few quick questions establish a visitor's style, then the wall transforms them live into their own generated artwork. They watch themselves become the campaign — and they film it happening.

applications.name: Interactive Game Wall
applications.headline: Everyone already knows the rules.
applications.description: Hit the targets, claim your squares on the LED screen, and race to three in a row. A game nobody needs explained keeps the queue moving and runs the competition by itself.

applications.name: Motion Reactive Wall
applications.headline: The wall answers movement.
applications.description: Flowers ripple and part as people pass, reacting to movement with no touch and no instruction. It reads as magic from a distance, which is what stops people walking past.

applications.name: Multi-Screen Installation
applications.headline: A wall of eyes that follows you.
applications.description: Dozens of screens, each showing a watchful eye that tracks people as they pass. Built to make digital harassment physically uncomfortable — an installation with an argument to make.

applications.name: Interactive Music Wall
applications.headline: Tap it and it plays.
applications.description: A wall of instruments anyone can play by touch — no skill required, no instructions, no queue discipline. Simple enough for a child and photogenic enough for the parent filming it.

applications.name: Interactive Light & Sound Tunnel
applications.headline: Every step reveals the next thing.
applications.description: Walking through triggers messages and sound that respond to where people are and how fast they move. A corridor stops being a corridor and becomes the reason to walk that way.

applications.name: Interactive Touch Catalogue
applications.headline: The whole range, at wall scale.
applications.description: A large touchscreen catalogue for browsing the range, switching language, and going deeper on whatever interests the visitor. Every session is logged, so you learn what people actually opened.

applications.name: Smart Cube
applications.headline: Turn the cube, change the story.
applications.description: A physical cube that drives the screen — rotate a face and the content switches. The interface is an object rather than a menu, so people pick it up without being invited to.

applications.name: Touch Interactive Screen
applications.headline: Point, press, explore.
applications.description: Large-format touch screens for stands and showrooms, running product content the visitor controls themselves.

applications.name: Motion Gesture Interactive Screen
applications.headline: Control it without touching it.
applications.description: Gesture-tracked screens that respond to hand and body movement from a distance — no surface to touch, nothing to clean between visitors.

applications.name: Interactive Product Detailing
applications.headline: The product explains itself.
applications.description: A guided interactive detailer that walks a visitor through a product's features at their own pace — built for environments where the claims have to be exact.

title: Immersive & holographic
note: Hardware that puts something in the room that is not really there — holograms, headsets and light in mid-air.

applications.name: Interactive Hologram
applications.headline: A life-size hologram that answers back.
applications.description: A 75-inch holographic unit with a bilingual AI avatar. A sensor wakes it as someone approaches; they speak, tap or press to ask, and it answers on-brand in Arabic or English — all day, unstaffed.

applications.name: VR Experience
applications.headline: Somewhere you cannot build on a stand.
applications.description: Headset experiences for the places a stand cannot contain — a plant, a finished development, the inside of a machine. Supervised, reset between guests, repeatable all day.

applications.name: Laser Cube
applications.headline: Light, cut into shape.
applications.description: A laser volume that draws geometry in mid-air inside a defined cube of space. Pure spectacle, readable from the other side of a hall.

applications.name: Hologram Fan
applications.headline: Awaiting content.
applications.description: Holographic fan display. No description or footage has been supplied yet — this card is a placeholder and will not go live until Hello Voice sends both.

applications.name: UV Camera
applications.headline: Awaiting content.
applications.description: A UV camera set up in pharmacy activations, showing what the eye cannot see on skin. Visitors see their own sun damage on screen, which makes the case for the product better than any claim on a shelf-talker.

title: Multimedia creation
note: Content built for a specific surface — an LED screen, a building, a stage, or a headset. The technique is in the making, not the hardware.

applications.name: 3D Naked Eye
applications.headline: Depth without glasses.
applications.description: Content built for LED screens that reads as genuine depth to the naked eye. No glasses and no app — the illusion works for anyone standing in roughly the right place.

applications.name: 3D Anamorphic Content
applications.headline: The screen that breaks its own frame.
applications.description: Anamorphic content matched to the exact shape of an LED screen, so the subject appears to lean out of it into the room. Engineered around the one viewing angle every phone films from.

applications.name: 3D Projection Mapping
applications.headline: Any surface becomes a screen.
applications.description: Projectors and purpose-built content that turn buildings, stages and objects into animated displays. The geometry is surveyed first, so the content fits what is actually there.

applications.name: Laser Mapping
applications.headline: Drawn in light, on the building.
applications.description: Synchronised lasers and animation projected onto real surfaces, turning architecture into a moving display. Reaches a scale and a brightness projection alone cannot.

applications.name: Stage Show Media
applications.headline: Content cut to the run of show.
applications.description: Stage visuals built to the timing of the event itself. The reveal lands on the beat because the content was made against the cue sheet rather than adapted to it afterwards.

applications.name: CGI Production
applications.headline: The product, before it exists.
applications.description: Full CGI for products and vehicles that cannot be filmed — because they are not built yet, or cannot be moved. Photoreal, and still usable long after the event is over.

applications.name: 360° Video
applications.headline: Look anywhere in the room.
applications.description: 360-degree film for onboarding and site familiarisation, where the viewer chooses where to look. Works in a headset or by dragging a finger across a phone.
